title.narrative: Youth Go Green PreCOP27 National Caravan

description.narrative:
Across Africa, communities, countries, and entire ecosystems are paying the price of global climate inaction. We are witnessing theeco-system collapse at a scale never seen before and the depletion of natural resources – the soil, water, and air humankind needs to survive – beyond the point of possible regeneration. But it doesn’t need to be this way. In Uganda in particular, climate change is causing unprecedented disasters that have resulted in colossal losses and damages including loss of lives. In November 2022 COP27will take place in Sharm-el-Sheikh, Egypt, and Oxfam will strive to ensure that political and financial commitments are met to meetthe high ambitions expressed in the last COP26 in Glasgow. Oxfam will push for a more inclusive and gender-transformative process in which action to respond to this existential threat happens when and where needed, which sees big emitters taking on their fair share of the burden by cutting emissions and helping pay for the climate response. This initiative will align with the objectives of the Oxfam advocacy strategy and contribute to the achievement of that, especially by ensuring that the voices of those most impacted by climate change are heard, through mobilizations, media, digital and financial support. The Caravan in Uganda is part of the Africapre-cop27 caravan that will facilitate citizens’ participation in policy spaces at national, regional and global levels to show howwomen and youth are leading their communities to become more resilient; where farmers are adapting their practices to protect food security and biodiversity; how indigenous groups are protecting eco-systems from collapse and how communities are finding ways to deal with the impacts of a crisis they are in no way responsible for. The people who are most impacted yet least responsible have something to say about it and governments across the world have a duty of care to listen and act. The Caravans to COP27 will support these groups in Uganda to be heard and push for action on adaptation and mitigation.
Overall change objective: Ensure the inclusion and engagement of communities most affected by climate change (women, youth, indigenous peoples) in the UNFCCC negotiation process (for instance on adaptation, loss and damage, agriculture etc.)
What? The Caravan to COP27 aims to connect people in Uganda and beyond. It is a movement of people (youth, women, and CSO actors). It’s a call for climate justice, justice for those least responsible, and most affected by climate change who are also the source of climate solutions and resilience leaders. The Caravan wants to see justice for those who suffer because of global climate inaction. The Caravan to COP27 is a way to mobilize, engage, connect and gatherperspectives and ideasof indigenous peoples, women, youth, farmers, grassroots communities, and natural resource movements. It’s away to engage and influence local and national decision-makers. It’s a way to bring the voices of those impacted by climate change like childrenand youth into the COP27 and will host a side event to share these perspectives. How? By supporting civil society to participate to get involved; supporting voices in the run-up to COP (eg. through the caravan); capacity building; lobbying with allieslike Women, Youth and Gender Constituency, and the African feminist taskforce for women and youth delegates to be part of government delegations to be heard by the parties engaged in the negotiation process.
The multi-stakeholders-organized Caravan running underthe concept of African climate caravans will ensure that community members/citizens are present at the meeting and have an opportunity to influence the discussions around the declaration. Oxfam is playing a facilitator role as we are building andstrengthening existing movements across the continent by bringing them into this initiative and using our networks and influence to amplify their voices. Children, Youth, and Women’s involvement The climate crisis has exposed children, youth, and womenon every continent to a greater risk of more destructive climate hazards, from heatwaves and droughts to floods, and landslides as well as an increase in pollution levels. The youth have been identified to lead this process and they are participating in providing interactive activities with all the young people across the Caravan journey to make sure that the voices of young people and women are heard at the Climate Change Summit (COP27) in Egypt. This youth-led initiative is a huge and comprehensive collective effort to advance environmental education and climate action for future generations. It is against this background that Oxfam in Uganda has identified Youth Go Green as a partner to organize and lead the Uganda Climate Caravan (UCC) with various activities during its journey. In essence, the Caravan roving the country would encourage young people to be fully engaged in the climate discussions and pave way for COP27 scheduled for November in Sharm El Sheikh. The Caravan’s agenda is to: Focus on hearing and amplifying people’s experiences, sharing solutions, learning from good practices, and influencing local and national governments. Specifically, the goals of the Caravans are to:  Mobilize local communities -including youth movements for climate justice and demand increased mobilization from African governments at COP27to address climate challenges in Africa.  Highlight the impacts of climate change on African communities and their environment  Highlight climate solutions integrated withtheir traditional and local knowledge.  Create a learning community of a) good practices and nature-based solutions for climate change adaptation, b) training of youth on climate negotiations in order to prepare them for participation in COY17 and COP27  Increase African citizen pressure on national governments and on international negotiations at COP27 to better take into account their realities, priorities, and aspirations. Youth Go Green will lead the caravan through the following activities; 1.Caravan routing from Kampala to Mbale through Palisa 2. Hold Climate marches in Palisa and Mbale 3. Engage youth in tree planting drive 4. Organise a Climate Change pre - Cop27 Dialogue. 5. Hold a pre- COP 27 Lobby meeting with Key stakeholders includingnational Negotiators
Methodology The Caravans are being designed and led by national Caravan Steering Committees made up of people knowledgeable about diverse communities' experience of climate impacts and who are responding with solutions. TheCaravans will first travel within each country. In October, the national caravans will last up to 10 days.
In Uganda, along the route of eastern Uganda, they will stop at places where the impacts of climate change can be experienced and where solutions thatare being led by communities can be found. They will build awareness of communities' perspectives and open opportunities to influence local authorities and central government. An equipped van will be led a team of young people traveling from Kampala, Jinja, via Pailsa up to Mbale city where the final caravan activities will climax.
In Sharm Al Sheik the Caravans will host a side event at the COP27 to engagedecision-makers and allies and encourage the sharing of experiences, ideas, and knowledgecollected through the Caravans.

participating-org.narrative:
1. HISTORY Why, when and by whom was the organisation founded? Explain the principal stages the organisation has been through and the major changes it has undergone, including changes in integrating gender.  Youth Go Green is the leading youth-led organization advancing climate action in Uganda. It was founded by Edwin Muhumuza in 2016 as an Umbrella organization of young people that are engaged in climate change, resilience, green growth, environment protection, SDGs, and youth empowerment-related activities in Uganda. Youth Go Green has a network and membership of over 500,000 youth members across the country in universities, schools, and youth-ledCBOs, CSOs, where 65% are female. These include; volunteers, trainees, support staff, and the technical team at the secretariat.  In 2017, Youth Go-Green (YGG) registered and acquired NGO status by the NGO Bureau under the Ministry of Internal Affairs and acquired a work permit No. 12738 to operate countrywide as a civil society NGO. It is also registered with the Registrar of Companies and was incorporated on the 16th day of September 2016 with a certificate of incorporation No.228811 in line with section 18(3) of the Company’s Act cap No.1/2012.
2. ACHIEVEMENTS What have been the principal resultsin the past three years that contribute to significant, structural, sustained and positive improvement in the lives of men, women, girls and boys suffering from poverty, injustice, insecurity and exclusion? • Effectively Mobilized and engaged more than twenty thousand youth across the country to participate in various climate change, environmental, and Sustainable Development Interventions. Mobilization of youth and communities to engage in biodiversity conservation activities such as tree planting, waste recycling for charcoal briquettes and provision of clean and safe water, implementation of water for production projects in collaboration with the Ministry of Water and Environment, National Forestry Authority (NFA) and other partners. • Building capacity and Mentoring Young Climate negotiators under the Global Climate Change processes that include training, dialogues and negotiations during Subsidiary Body meetings and Conference of the Parties organized by under the auspices of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) with support of Uganda Government, UNDP, andother Development partners. • Since 2016 have organized Six (6) National level and African level Youth Conferences on climate change and its linkages with the SDGsin Uganda mainly funded by Government, UNDP and FAO. This regional conference brought together more than 1,000 African Youth in a single space of discussion on challenges, opportunities and prospects in advancing solutions to climate change, Biodiversityconservation and SDGs. • Secured and Signed a five-year Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Waterand Environment for meaningful empowerment of Youth in Climate Change, wetland restoration, and Green livelihood improvement. • Under Innovative Youth Engagement in waste management, more than 250 Youth were trained and skilled in strengthening Behavioral change among youth to control the spread of COVID 19 and its fatality with a focus on adherence to SOPs in institutions and communities including effective waste management in Kampala and Gulu city. • Organized successful Youth-led policy advocacy, and dialogues on climate change in partnership and with support from key development partners such as OXFAM, UNDP, WWF, SEATIN, and Disaster Reduction andPreparedness Department in the Office of the Prime Minister tackling climate-induced disasters through youth engagement. For instance, a youth position paper and policy briefs were recently presented to the Climate Committee of Parliament contributing to the recent Climate change act and bill. • Recently planted over 15,000 bamboos for Restoration of River Rwizi trees with support from WWF aspart of a biodiversity conservation campaign. • Youth Go Green launched Go-Green clubs in primary and secondary schools as well as chapters in Universities. These interventions are meant to create awareness of climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, advocacy, and waste recycling for charcoal briquettes production among others.
3. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE Mission:
“Empower and engage young people in pursuance of low-carbon socio-economic development pathway”
Institutional objectives:
• To identify and mobilize young people and communities for participation in the organization’s Thematic areas. • To equip young people with appropriate information, knowledge, and skills. • To build the capacity of youth in advocacy and lobbying. • To ensure inclusion/mainstreaming ofResilience in all relevant laws, policies, guidelines, regulations, and institutional arrangements. • To establish partnerships andnetworks with Government and other development partners and institutions to support and strengthen youth engagement and participation. • To engage and include the young people in environmentally friendly and disaster risk reduction interventions. • To mobilize requisite and adequate resources to fulfill the organization’s mission. • To promote and support national and international initiatives for the achievement of SDGs and climate change action • To ensure inclusion of gender and inter-generational equity in all efforts. • To promote good governance and protection of rights of all stakeholders
Field(s) of activity: What are the principal thematic and geographic areas in which the organization works?
 Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation  Biodiversity Conservation <(>&<)> DRR  Green Growth and Energy Transition  Innovation and Advocacy  Youth skilling and Empowerment
4. STRATEGIC POSITIONING Analyse the environment in which the organisation works? Who are the other relevant social actors, including government and business, and what roles do they play? ' In this context, what is unique about the position of the organisation?
Youth Go Green is currently developing her 5year Strategic Plan which is intended to build staff awareness and capacity on youth-related issues. The Strategy aims to facilitate increased impact and expanded global, regional, and country-level action to address the needs, and advance therightsof young people in all their diversity, and ensure their engagement and meaningful participation in the implementation, review, andfollow-up of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development as well as other relevant global and country agendas and frameworks.
